title: Possessive Adjectives - My, Your, His, Her
description: Show who owns what: 'my book', 'his cat', 'their house' - essential vocabulary!
can_do: Show ownership (my cat, your house, his book, their car)
Use possessive adjectives with correct gender agreement
Say 'Where is my book?' or 'I want your car' in French

vocabulary.note: masculine form - mon livre, mon père, mon ami
feminine form - ma maison, ma mère, ma voiture
plural form - mes chats, mes livres, mes amis
masculine form - ton chat, ton frère, ton travail
feminine form - ta voiture, ta sœur, ta chambre
plural form - tes amis, tes parents, tes chaussures
masculine form - son livre, son chien, son bureau
feminine form - sa maison, sa fille, sa cuisine
plural form - ses chats, ses enfants, ses clés
singular form - notre maison, notre école, notre jardin
plural form - nos chats, nos vacances, nos professeurs
singular form - votre livre, votre famille, votre bureau
plural form - vos livres, vos enfants, vos bagages
singular form - leur chat, leur maison, leur projet
plural form - leurs chats, leurs amis, leurs idées

concepts.definition: These words say whose something is. They go right before the noun, where {le} or {un} would go.

examples.fr: Je vais au café avec mon ami.
examples.en: I'm going to the café with my friend.

concepts.definition: The possessive takes the gender and number of the thing owned, never of the owner.
Use the {tu} words for your with a friend, and the {vous} words with someone you do not know or with a group.
Our, your and their have no masculine or feminine forms. They change only for the plural.
My, your and his or her have three forms: masculine, feminine and plural. Our, your and their have two: singular and plural.

items.situation: You're talking about your father. Which possessive?
items.hint: Your possession, père is masculine - check vocab table!

items.situation: You're talking about your mother. Which possessive?
items.hint: Your possession, mère is feminine - check vocab table!

items.situation: You're talking about your books (multiple). Which possessive?
items.hint: Your possession, livres is plural - check vocab table!

mistakes.feedback: That's singular masculine 'my' - livres is plural
That's singular feminine 'my' - livres is plural

items.situation: Talking to a friend about their brother. Which possessive?
items.hint: Friend's possession, frère is masculine - informal form

mistakes.feedback: That's formal 'your' - use informal with friends

items.situation: Talking to a friend about their sister. Which possessive?
items.hint: Friend's possession, sœur is feminine - informal form

mistakes.feedback: That's formal 'your' - use informal with friends

items.situation: Talking to a friend about their parents. Which possessive?
items.hint: Friend's possession, parents is plural - informal form

mistakes.feedback: That's singular masculine 'your' - parents is plural
That's formal 'your' - use informal with friends

items.situation: Talking about Marie's dog (masculine). Which possessive?
items.hint: Marie owns it, chien is masculine - matches the thing owned!

items.situation: Talking about Pierre's house (feminine). Which possessive?
items.hint: Pierre owns it, maison is feminine - matches the thing owned!

items.situation: Talking about someone's children. Which possessive?
items.hint: Third person owner, enfants is plural

mistakes.feedback: That's singular masculine 'his/her' - enfants is plural
That's singular feminine 'his/her' - enfants is plural

items.situation: Talking about the house you and your family share. Which possessive?
items.hint: Group possession, maison is singular - notre/nos?

items.situation: Talking about the vacations you and your family take. Which possessive?
items.hint: Group possession, vacances is plural - notre/nos?

items.situation: Speaking formally to someone about their office. Which possessive?
items.hint: Formal situation, bureau is singular - votre/vos?

items.situation: Speaking formally to someone about their luggage. Which possessive?
items.hint: Formal situation, bagages is plural - votre/vos?

items.situation: Talking about a project owned by a group of people. Which possessive?
items.hint: They own it, projet is singular - leur/leurs?

items.situation: Talking about ideas owned by a group of people. Which possessive?
items.hint: They own them, idées is plural - leur/leurs?
